checks: The w=0, β=1 test yields t≤M. After identifying the facet with its intrinsic Euclidean space, the compact convex fixed-mass moment body and upper-cap support formula apply there. For a mass-t selector, the hinge bound follows from θ(w·x+δ)≤[w·x+δ]₊. Proper nonflat quantile, constant direction, and full mass all provide an attaining threshold.

Substitution δ=β−w·y gives the stated dual inequality with coefficient 2t+s. Separation gives equivalence with moment membership. The cutting levels imply u·b_*=t(u·y−α), so the prescribed moment is in the correct affine plane. Expanding the selector equation gives precisely the unnormalized moment.

For t<M, each unit tangential direction has one proper volume-t level, since every open slab between support levels has positive facet volume and cutting hyperplanes are null intrinsically. Bounded levels, dominated convergence and uniqueness give continuity of cap centroids. Their compact convex hull has the same support as the moment body; intrinsic Carathéodory uses at most d cap means. A constant selector is strictly below the support in every nonflat direction, giving relative interior by compactness. Every relative boundary mean has a nonflat support direction, and the equality case in the hinge integrand forces its cap indicator uniquely almost everywhere.

At t=M the only selector is one a.e. If s=t, midpoint inclusion and Brunn–Minkowski force equality of all three section areas, and proper inclusion between full-dimensional compact convex bodies in the same cutting plane would strictly increase measure. Equality in Brunn–Minkowski gives translates, with equal lengths handling dimension one. The centroid of their midpoint is (c_A+c_F)/2; the moment equation then gives y=c_K.

Projection to the compact convex moment body gives support value w·p for w=b_*−p and residual support gap −‖b_*−p‖². The hinge threshold attains this gap; the actual fixed-body right derivative divides it by ‖u‖. Both points lie in the same affine moment plane, so w is tangent. Negative derivative implies strict decrease for every sufficiently small positive size.

dependencies.hypotheses: Use compact convex fixed-mass means and proof formula (1) with dimension d−1, body equal to the facet transported by affine isometry, mass t≤M, and the projected tangential direction. A flat ambient direction is constant on the facet and is handled explicitly.
Use the local single-body right derivative formulas from the proof for proper A,K and outside-supporting B. The perturbation is affine at each fiber and divided with the old margin by ‖u‖.

overlap.comparison: Its compact moment-body and upper-cap support results apply to the intrinsic facet. The new result identifies the cap-dependent prescribed moment, the exact fixed-mark first-order equivalence, and the geometric descent and rigidity consequences.
Its proof consumes the interval version for three planar globally minimizing rows. It does not give the general-dimensional moment equivalence or quantitative nearest-point descent.

readability: The normalized derivative and the unnormalized moment are tracked separately. The coefficient 2t+s is verified by substitution.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The exact moment condition characterizes the fixed-mark first-order inequalities and gives selector representation, rigidity at full mass and explicit strict descent outside the moment body.
